userStories.title: Protocol contract, capability and read-only mint
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the additive protocol types, the `projectCode` capability parsing, a read-only GitHub installation token mint, and a read-only mode on `GitTokenBroker.mint`.

**Motivation** — A PROJECT thread's agent cannot see any code today; reading every repository of the project needs a repo-scoped, read-only brokered token and a capability to gate it (S5b-R15).

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

- 1c-b-D1 (protocol, additive): `@nathapp/fleet-protocol` gains, in `packages/fleet-protocol/src/threads.ts`, `ProjectRepoAssign { repoId: string; owner: string; name: string; defaultBranch: string; cloneUrl: string }`, `ProjectRepoUnavailable { owner: string; name: string; reason: 'not a GitHub repository' | 'no installation' | 'limit' }`, `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS = { maxRepos: 10, maxUnavailable: 50 } as const`, and `ThreadAssign` gains the optional `projectRepos?: ProjectRepoAssign[]` and `projectReposUnavailable?: ProjectRepoUnavailable[]`. In `packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts`, `TokenRequest`, `GitToken` and `GitTokenError` gain an optional `repoId?: string`, and `RunnerCapabilities` gains `projectCode?: true`. (The runner's parseAssign rules for these entries belong to US-004.) `FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is unchanged: every field is optional and an older peer ignores it. The API reads the package with `import type` only (`apps/api/src/fleet/common/protocol.spec.ts:36-41`), so `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS` is mirrored as a runtime constant in `apps/api/src/fleet/common/thread-jobs.ts`, as `THREAD_LIMITS` is (`:24`), and a spec pins the two equal. The new threads exports are re-exported from `packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts`.
- 1c-b-D2 (capability): `parseCapabilitiesCore` (`apps/api/src/fleet/common/capabilities-core.ts:118-165`) accepts `projectCode` exactly as `kodaTools`: absent or `true`, anything else fails with reason `projectCode`, and only `true` is kept.
- 1c-b-D3 (read-only mint): `GitHubAppClient` gains `mintReadOnlyToken(installationId: bigint, repoName: string): Promise<{ token: string; expiresAt: Date }>`, which posts to the same `access_tokens` endpoint as `mintInstallationToken` (`github-app-client.ts:61-72`) with `repositories: [repoName]` and `permissions: { contents: 'read', metadata: 'read' }`, and maps the response exactly as `mintInstallationToken` does (404 `app_not_installed`, 403/422 `app_permissions_insufficient`, other non-201 or a malformed body `provider_error`). `mintInstallationToken` is unchanged.
- 1c-b-D4 (broker): `GitTokenBroker.mint` (`git-token.broker.ts:30-45`) takes `{ jobId; leaseEpoch; repo; readOnly?: boolean }`. With `readOnly: true` the cache key is `${jobId}:${leaseEpoch}:ro:${repo.id}`, `fresh` calls `mintReadOnlyToken` for a GitHub repository, throws `RepoCheckException('app_not_installed')` when `githubInstallationId` is null, and throws `RepoCheckException('provider_error')` for any other provider; the returned `GitToken` and any `GitTokenError` carry `repoId: repo.id`. Without `readOnly` the key, the mint and the result are as today. `evict(jobId)` already drops every key starting `${jobId}:`, so it drops read-only entries too.

**Scope** — In: protocol types/exports, api runtime mirror of PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS, capability parsing, mintReadOnlyToken, broker readOnly mode. Out: sync fence and parser (US-002), ASSIGN building/placement (US-003), all runner and web work.

**Interface**
```typescript
interface ProjectRepoAssign { repoId: string; owner: string; name: string; defaultBranch: string; cloneUrl: string }
interface ProjectRepoUnavailable { owner: string; name: string; reason: 'not a GitHub repository' | 'no installation' | 'limit' }
const PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS = { maxRepos: 10, maxUnavailable: 50 } as const
// ThreadAssign: projectRepos?: ProjectRepoAssign[]; projectReposUnavailable?: ProjectRepoUnavailable[]
// TokenRequest / GitToken / GitTokenError: repoId?: string
// RunnerCapabilities: projectCode?: true
GitHubAppClient.mintReadOnlyToken(installationId: bigint, repoName: string): Promise<{ token: string; expiresAt: Date }>
GitTokenBroker.mint(req: { jobId; leaseEpoch; repo; readOnly?: boolean }, now?)
```
acceptanceCriteria: The API's runtime `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS` from `apps/api/src/fleet/common/thread-jobs.ts` deep-equals the `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS` exported by `@nathapp/fleet-protocol`, which is `{ maxRepos: 10, maxUnavailable: 50 }`.
`parseCapabilitiesCore` on a valid capability object with `projectCode: true` returns an object whose `projectCode` is `true`.
`parseCapabilitiesCore` on a valid capability object without `projectCode` returns an object with no `projectCode` key.
`parseCapabilitiesCore` on a valid capability object with `projectCode: false` throws `CapabilityValidationError` with reason `projectCode`.

`GitHubAppClient.mintReadOnlyToken(42n, 'sandbox')` against the fake forge posts to `/app/installations/42/access_tokens` a body whose `repositories` is `['sandbox']` and whose `permissions` is exactly `{ contents: 'read', metadata: 'read' }`, and resolves the forge's `token` and `expires_at` as `{ token, expiresAt }`.

`GitHubAppClient.mintReadOnlyToken` throws `RepoCheckException` with reason `app_not_installed` when the forge answers 404, `app_permissions_insufficient` when it answers 403 and when it answers 422, and `provider_error` when it answers 500 and when it answers 201 with a body lacking `token` (one table-driven test).

`GitTokenBroker.mint({ jobId: 'j1', leaseEpoch: 2, repo, readOnly: true })` for a GitHub repository with installation `7n` calls `mintReadOnlyToken(7n, repo.name)`, never `mintInstallationToken`, and resolves a token whose `jobId` is `j1` and `repoId` is `repo.id`.
After a read-only `mint` for job `j1` epoch 2, a `mint` for `j1` epoch 2 without `readOnly` calls `mintInstallationToken` (the read-only entry is not reused).
A second read-only `mint` for the same job, epoch and repository within the reuse margin calls no GitHub method and resolves the cached token.

`GitTokenBroker.mint` with `readOnly: true` for a GitHub repository whose `githubInstallationId` is null resolves `{ ok: false, error: { jobId, repoId, reason: 'app_not_installed' } }` and calls no GitHub method.
`GitTokenBroker.mint` with `readOnly: true` for a GitLab repository resolves an error with reason `provider_error` and calls neither `mintReadOnlyToken` nor the GitLab token source.
After a read-only `mint` and a write `mint` for job `j1`, `evict('j1')` makes the next `mint` of each call GitHub again.
Read-only `mint` for repository `r1` and then for repository `r2` of the same job and epoch calls `mintReadOnlyToken` twice, and each resolved token carries its own `repoId`.

routing.reasoning: Token minting and credential scoping (security override) across protocol package, capability parser and broker; patterns mirror existing kodaTools and mintInstallationToken code.

modifiedFiles.reason: outside the api package: gains `ProjectRepoAssign`, `ProjectRepoUnavailable`, `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS` and the optional `ThreadAssign` fields `projectRepos` and `projectReposUnavailable` (1c-b-D1); additive only.

outside the api package: `TokenRequest`, `GitToken`, `GitTokenError` gain `repoId?: string`, `RunnerCapabilities` gains `projectCode?: true`, and the new threads exports are re-exported (1c-b-D1); additive only.

userStories.title: Read-only token fence on sync
userStories.description:
Every `SyncService.sync` case below runs with a stubbed job repository, fence and `GitTokenBroker`, a held RUNNING `THREAD` job `j1` of project `p1` (epoch 1) whose `findThreadTokenScope` resolves `{ kind: 'PROJECT', action: 'SESSION' }` unless stated, `findProjectRepos('p1')` resolving `[r1 (GitHub, installation 1)]` unless stated, and a sync body whose `tokenRequests` holds the request.

**Goal** — Let the sync endpoint grant per-repository read-only tokens, fenced by a recomputed scope, and validate `repoId` on token requests.

**Motivation** — The runner must obtain a read-only token per project repository, and the API must never mint one for a repository the session's ASSIGN did not list (no stored record of the ASSIGN exists).

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

- 1c-b-D5 (token fence): there is no stored record of which repositories an ASSIGN listed (`FleetCommand.payload` is written once; `grantTokens` reads only the job row, `apps/api/src/fleet/sync/sync.service.ts:112-141`). The fence therefore recomputes the scope. `grantTokens`'s request type gains `repoId?: string`. A request with `repoId` passes today's checks first, unchanged (unknown job -> `unknownJobIds`; fence not held -> `FenceService.abandon`; state not in `RUNNER_HELD_STATES` -> `job_not_active`, with `repoId` echoed on the error). It is then granted only when also (a) `job.command` is `THREAD`, (b) a new `IFleetJobRepository.findThreadTokenScope(jobId): Promise<{ kind: 'REPO' | 'PROJECT'; action: string } | null>` resolves kind `PROJECT` and action `SESSION`, and (c) the request's `repoId` is one of `fetchableProjectRepos(await findProjectRepos(job.projectId))` (1c-b-D7, created by US-003), the same walk the ASSIGN used, so a repository the ASSIGN listed as unavailable (GitLab, no installation, beyond the cap) or a repository of another project is never granted. Any failure of (a)-(c) answers a `GitTokenError` `{ jobId, repoId, reason: 'repo_not_assigned' }` and mints nothing. Granted requests mint through `broker.mint({ jobId, leaseEpoch, repo, readOnly: true })`, `repo` being the matching `FleetRepoRef` from that list, outside the transaction, as today. The public entry point is `SyncService.sync(runnerId, raw)` (`sync.service.ts:54`), which calls `grantTokens` at `:96`.
- 1c-b-D6 (sync parser): `parseTokenRequest` (`apps/api/src/fleet/sync/sync-request.parser.ts:58-61`) keeps `repoId` when it is a string of 1 to 64 characters and fails with reason `tokenRequest` for any other present value. A request without `repoId` is exactly as today. The 64-request cap (`SYNC_LIMITS.tokenRequests`) is unchanged.

A new `IFleetJobRepository.findThreadTokenScope(jobId)` is implemented in `PrismaFleetJobRepository` (the only implementer). The `repoId` response is echoed on `gitTokens` (carrying `repoId`) and `gitTokenErrors`. Requests without `repoId` call `GitTokenBroker.mint` with `{ jobId, leaseEpoch, repo }` (no `readOnly` key), `repo` being `findRepo(job.repoId)`, exactly as today.

**Scope** — In: parseTokenRequest repoId, grantTokens fence, findThreadTokenScope (interface + Prisma impl), unit test file sync-token-fence.spec.ts. Out: `fetchableProjectRepos` / `findProjectRepos` implementation (US-003, SEAM-0), broker/mint (US-001), runner side.

**Interface**
```typescript
IFleetJobRepository.findThreadTokenScope(jobId: string): Promise<{ kind: 'REPO' | 'PROJECT'; action: string } | null>
SyncService.grantTokens(runnerId, requests: ReadonlyArray<{ jobId; leaseEpoch; repoId?: string }>, now)
// GitTokenError for denied repoId requests: { jobId, repoId, reason: 'repo_not_assigned' | 'job_not_active' }
```
acceptanceCriteria: `parseSyncRequest` keeps `repoId: 'r1'` on a token request that carries it, and returns a token request without a `repoId` key when it is absent.
`parseSyncRequest` throws a validation error with reason `tokenRequest` for a token request whose `repoId` is an empty string, a number, or a 65-character string (one table-driven test).

`SyncService.sync` with a request `{ jobId: 'j1', leaseEpoch: 1, repoId: 'r1' }` calls `findProjectRepos` with `p1` and calls `GitTokenBroker.mint` once with `{ jobId: 'j1', leaseEpoch: 1, repo, readOnly: true }` where `repo.id` is `r1`.
For that request, the sync response's `gitTokens` holds the broker's token, carrying `repoId: 'r1'`.

`SyncService.sync` with a `repoId` request naming a repository that `findProjectRepos('p1')` does not return (another project's) answers a `gitTokenErrors` entry `{ jobId: 'j1', repoId, reason: 'repo_not_assigned' }` and calls `GitTokenBroker.mint` zero times.
`SyncService.sync` with a `repoId` request on a job whose `findThreadTokenScope` resolves `{ kind: 'REPO', action: 'SESSION' }` answers `repo_not_assigned` and calls `mint` zero times.
`SyncService.sync` with a `repoId` request on a PROJECT thread job whose turn action is `PUBLISH` answers `repo_not_assigned`.
`SyncService.sync` with a `repoId` request on a held `RUN` job answers `repo_not_assigned` and never calls `findThreadTokenScope`.
With `findProjectRepos('p1')` resolving 11 installed GitHub repositories, a `repoId` request naming the 11th answers `repo_not_assigned`, and one naming the 10th is minted.
With `findProjectRepos('p1')` resolving a GitLab repository `g1` and a GitHub repository `n1` with no installation, `repoId` requests for `g1` and for `n1` each answer `repo_not_assigned`.
`SyncService.sync` with a `repoId` request on a job held by this runner in state `COMPLETED` answers `{ jobId: 'j1', repoId: 'r1', reason: 'job_not_active' }` and calls `mint` zero times.
`SyncService.sync` with a token request without `repoId` on a held RUN job calls `GitTokenBroker.mint` with `{ jobId, leaseEpoch, repo }` (no `readOnly` key), `repo` being `findRepo(job.repoId)`.
`SyncService.sync` with a `repoId` request whose fence does not hold (another runner's lease) calls `FenceService.abandon` and calls `mint` zero times.

`PrismaFleetJobRepository.findThreadTokenScope` for a THREAD job of a PROJECT thread whose turn action is `SESSION` resolves `{ kind: 'PROJECT', action: 'SESSION' }`, and for a RUN job with no thread turn resolves null.

routing.reasoning: Access-control fence on token minting (security override); recomputed scope must exactly match the ASSIGN walk and fail closed.

suggestedCriteria: `SyncService.sync` with a `repoId` request for an unknown job id adds the job id to `unknownJobIds` and calls `mint` zero times.
outOfScope: Implementing `fetchableProjectRepos` and `findProjectRepos` belongs to US-003 (SEAM-0); this story only calls them.

userStories.title: PROJECT ASSIGN repositories, session notice and instructions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Have placement list the project's repositories in a PROJECT session ASSIGN, record a session notice when the runner lacks `projectCode`, and update PROJECT instructions to mention the code tools.

**Motivation** — The agent must be told which repositories to read, a runner without the capability must degrade visibly, and the instructions currently say 'You have no repository'.

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

- 1c-b-D7 (ASSIGN repositories): `apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/project-repos-assign.ts` exports two pure functions. `fetchableProjectRepos(repos: readonly FleetRepoRef[]): FleetRepoRef[]` returns, in input order, the GitHub repositories with a non-null `githubInstallationId`, at most `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS.maxRepos` of them. `withProjectRepos(thread: ThreadAssign, repos: readonly FleetRepoRef[], vcs: { githubApiUrl: string; gitlabApiUrl: string }): ThreadAssign` builds `projectRepos` from `fetchableProjectRepos(repos)` and walks `repos` in the given order: a non-GitHub repository is unavailable `not a GitHub repository`; a GitHub repository with a null `githubInstallationId` is unavailable `no installation`; any other repository is added to `projectRepos` as `{ repoId, owner, name, defaultBranch, cloneUrl: cloneUrlFor(repo, vcs) }` until `projectRepos` holds `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS.maxRepos` entries, and each later one is unavailable `limit`. `projectReposUnavailable` keeps its first `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS.maxUnavailable` entries. It returns the thread with both arrays set (possibly empty). `PlacementService.assign` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/placement.service.ts:189-202`, private; reached from the public `placeJob(jobId)` at `:62`) applies it after `withKodaTools` only when the thread's `kind` is `PROJECT`, its `action` is `SESSION` and the runner's `capabilities.projectCode === true`; only then does it call a new `IFleetJobRepository.findProjectRepos(projectId): Promise<FleetRepoRef[]>` with `job.projectId`, ordered by `createdAt` ascending then `id` ascending (the anchor order, `apps/api/src/fleet/repos/prisma-fleet-repo.repository.ts:37-40`) and bounded by `take: PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS.maxRepos + PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS.maxUnavailable` (60; rule api-data). `vcs` is the `vcsConfig` `PlacementService` already injects (`:44`). `cloneUrlFor(repo, cfg)` is in `apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/clone-url.ts:10`.
- 1c-b-D8 (session notice): `PrismaThreadIngestRepository` records `projectCodeUnavailableOn: <runner name>` in the stored session on `session_started` when the thread's kind, read in that branch with `chatThread.findUnique({ where: { id: threadId }, select: { kind: true } })` (`ChatThread.kind`, default `REPO`), is `PROJECT` and the hosting runner's capabilities lack `projectCode: true`, beside `kodaToolsUnavailableOn` (`prisma-thread-ingest.repository.ts:419-433, 472-480`), and keeps it on close or failure under the same rule as `kodaToolsUnavailableOn` (`:442-448`). A REPO thread never gets it. The field joins `StoredSession`, the domain session type (`chat-thread.domain.ts:50-51`) and the `session` schema in `thread.dto.ts:27`. The thread GET routes pass the stored session through unchanged.
- 1c-b-D9 (instructions): the line of `buildProjectThreadInstructions` after the role line and any brief lines (`thread-instructions.ts:45`) becomes: `Ask one question at a time. You have no shell and no web access. You read the project's code only through list_repos, list_files, search_repo and read_file when they are available (read-only, pinned at session start); cite code as owner/name:path@sha7 and never claim facts about code you have not read.` The role line and `KODA_TOOLS_LINE` are unchanged. REPO instructions are unchanged.

US-003 regenerates `openapi.json` with `bun run api:export-spec` and the generated clients with `bun run generate` for the session field (never hand-edit generated files). Existing tests to update: `thread-instructions.spec.ts` (exact second-line assertion at `:99-101` takes the D9 text; the assertion at `:88-91` that `list_files` and `search_repo` never appear in PROJECT instructions is narrowed to `write_doc` and `Publish`), and `prisma-thread-ingest.repository.spec.ts` fake thread row (`:33-41`) gains `kind` (default `REPO`).

**Scope** — In: project-repos-assign.ts, findProjectRepos (interface + Prisma impl), placement wiring, session_started notice + StoredSession/domain/DTO field, instructions line, openapi/CLI regeneration. Out: the token fence (US-002), runner ASSIGN parsing (US-004), web notice (US-008).

**Interface**
```typescript
fetchableProjectRepos(repos: readonly FleetRepoRef[]): FleetRepoRef[]
withProjectRepos(thread: ThreadAssign, repos: readonly FleetRepoRef[], vcs: { githubApiUrl: string; gitlabApiUrl: string }): ThreadAssign
IFleetJobRepository.findProjectRepos(projectId: string): Promise<FleetRepoRef[]>
// session: projectCodeUnavailableOn?: string
```
acceptanceCriteria: `withProjectRepos(thread, [a (GitHub, installation 1), b (GitLab), c (GitHub, no installation)], vcs)` returns a thread whose `projectRepos` is `[{ repoId: a.id, owner: a.owner, name: a.name, defaultBranch: a.defaultBranch, cloneUrl }]`, with `cloneUrl` equal to `cloneUrlFor(a, vcs)`.
For that input, `projectReposUnavailable` is `[{ owner: b.owner, name: b.name, reason: 'not a GitHub repository' }, { owner: c.owner, name: c.name, reason: 'no installation' }]`, in input order.
`withProjectRepos` with 12 installed GitHub repositories returns 10 `projectRepos` (the first 10 in input order) and 2 `projectReposUnavailable` entries with reason `limit`.
`withProjectRepos` with 60 GitLab repositories returns an empty `projectRepos` and exactly 50 `projectReposUnavailable` entries.

`PrismaFleetJobRepository.findProjectRepos(projectId)` returns the project's repositories ordered by `createdAt` ascending and, on equal `createdAt`, by `id` ascending, none of another project, and at most 60 of a project with 61.

`PlacementService.placeJob` of a queued PROJECT `SESSION` THREAD job onto the only eligible runner, whose capabilities hold `projectCode: true`, calls `findProjectRepos` with the job's `projectId` and creates an ASSIGN command whose `payload.thread.projectRepos` lists that stub's installed GitHub repositories.
`PlacementService.placeJob` of the same job onto a runner without `projectCode` creates an ASSIGN whose `payload.thread` has no `projectRepos` key and never calls `findProjectRepos`.

`PlacementService.placeJob` of a REPO `SESSION` THREAD job onto a runner with `projectCode: true` creates an ASSIGN whose `payload.thread` has no `projectRepos` key and never calls `findProjectRepos`.
Folding a `session_started` line for a PROJECT thread hosted by a runner whose capabilities lack `projectCode` stores a session whose `projectCodeUnavailableOn` is the runner's name.
Folding a `session_started` line for a PROJECT thread on a runner with `projectCode: true`, and for a REPO thread on a runner without it, stores a session with no `projectCodeUnavailableOn` key.
After a session with `projectCodeUnavailableOn` closes, the stored session of that job keeps `projectCodeUnavailableOn`.
`GET /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id` of a PROJECT thread whose stored session holds `projectCodeUnavailableOn: 'wk-mac'` answers a body whose `data.session.projectCodeUnavailableOn` is `wk-mac`.

`buildProjectThreadInstructions({ project: 'sandbox', skills: [] })` returns text whose line after the role line is exactly the 1c-b-D9 line, which names `list_repos`, `list_files`, `search_repo` and `read_file` and the citation form `owner/name:path@sha7`.
`buildProjectThreadInstructions` returns text with no `write_doc` and no `Publish`, and `buildThreadInstructions` for a REPO thread returns text with no `list_repos` and no `read_file`.

routing.reasoning: Several files but each change follows an existing pattern (withKodaTools placement gating, kodaToolsUnavailableOn ingest fold, DTO field); no new abstraction and no token or credential handling.

suggestedCriteria: `withProjectRepos` with no repositories returns a thread whose `projectRepos` and `projectReposUnavailable` are both empty arrays.

modifiedFiles.reason: the exact second-line assertion at `:99-101` takes the 1c-b-D9 text, and the assertion at `:88-91` that `list_files` and `search_repo` never appear in PROJECT instructions is narrowed to `write_doc` and `Publish`, since the new line names the PROJECT code tools; other assertions unchanged.
outside the api package: regenerated by `bun run api:export-spec` for the `session.projectCodeUnavailableOn` field.
outside the api package: regenerated by `bun run generate` for the same field; never hand-edited.
its fake thread row (`:33-41`) gains `kind` (default `REPO`) so the `session_started` branch can read it; the existing `kodaToolsUnavailableOn` expectations (`:459`, `:503`) are unchanged.

outOfScope: GitLab repositories are not read by PROJECT threads (1c-b-R2); they are only listed as unavailable `not a GitHub repository`.
The token fence and `findThreadTokenScope` belong to US-002; the web notice belongs to US-008.

userStories.title: Runner ASSIGN parsing, per-repository tokens and capability
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Teach the runner to parse project repositories from the ASSIGN, hold and serve a read-only token per repository, and advertise `projectCode`.

**Motivation** — The session start needs per-repository credentials and the API only places code-capable sessions on runners that report the capability.

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

- 1c-b-D1 (runner parse rule): the runner's `parseAssign` accepts a `projectRepos` entry only when `repoId` passes `assertSegment` and is at most 64 characters, `owner` passes `assertOwner`, `name` passes `assertSegment`, `defaultBranch` is a non-empty string of at most 255 characters (the rule `parseAssign` applies to `repo.defaultBranch`), and `cloneUrl` parses as a URL whose protocol is `https:` (stricter than `assertCloneUrl`, which also accepts `http:` and `file:`); a `projectReposUnavailable` entry needs an `owner` passing `assertOwner`, a `name` passing `assertSegment` and one of the three reasons. Malformed input (not an array, over `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS.maxRepos` entries, any bad entry, `projectReposUnavailable` malformed or over `PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS.maxUnavailable`, or `projectRepos` on a REPO thread) refuses the ASSIGN with `invalid project repos`.
- 1c-b-D2 (capability): The runner's `NaxCapabilityProbe` (`apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.ts:165-174`) reports `projectCode: true` next to `kodaTools: true`. The runner already refuses to start on git older than 2.30 (`assertMinGitVersion`, `apps/runner/src/daemon/daemon.ts:102`), which covers every git command this feature runs, so the probe adds no version check. `StaticCapabilityProbe` is unchanged.
- 1c-b-D10 (runner tokens per repository): `TokenCache` (`apps/runner/src/credentials/token-cache.ts`) keys an entry by `${jobId}:${leaseEpoch}` without a repository and `${jobId}:${leaseEpoch}:${repoId}` with one; `want`, `wanted`, `drop` and `state` gain an optional last parameter `repoId?: string`. `requests` keeps the highest epoch per `(jobId, repoId)`, includes `repoId` in each request that has one, and orders the requests it returns: every entry without `repoId` first, then repository entries in the order they were first wanted; it still returns at most `MAX_TOKEN_REQUESTS` (64), and the rest wait for a later sync. `apply` matches a token or error to the requested entry by `(jobId, repoId)`, building its request-epoch lookup keyed by `(jobId, repoId)` as well. `buildSyncRequest` (`apps/runner/src/sync/batch.ts:74`) keeps `repoId` when present. Entries without `repoId` behave exactly as today.
- 1c-b-D11 (runner credentials per repository): `CredentialBroker` (`apps/runner/src/credentials/broker.ts`) implements a new interface `RepoCredentialProvider { acquireRepo(job: JobRow, repo: { repoId: string; cloneUrl: string }, options: AcquireOptions): Promise<AcquireResult>; releaseRepo(job: JobRow, repoId: string): Promise<void> }`. `acquireRepo` works as `acquire` but calls `tokens.want(jobId, leaseEpoch, repoId)`, serves a socket at `socketPathFor(socketDir, runnerId, jobId, leaseEpoch, repoId)` whose reply reads `wanted` and `state` with that `repoId` and answers only for the protocol and host of `repo.cloneUrl`, writes no `gh`/`glab` shims, and returns `binDir: null`; a wait that ends without a token returns the same reasons `acquire` does (`git token: <reason>`, `git token: timeout`, `cancelled`). The broker records each acquired `repoId` per `(jobId, leaseEpoch)`. `releaseRepo` drops that token, closes that socket and forgets the record; `release(job)` also releases every recorded repository of the job. `socketPathFor` (`apps/runner/src/credentials/socket-dir.ts:21-24`) hashes `${runnerId}:${jobId}:${leaseEpoch}` as today, and `${runnerId}:${jobId}:${leaseEpoch}:${repoId}` when `repoId` is given (sha256, first 16 hex characters, `.sock`). `helperValue(self, sock)` is in `credentials/job-files.ts:11-13`; `CredentialServer.listen` in `cred-server.ts:56`; `ensureSocketDir` in `socket-dir.ts:30`.

US-004 also updates `apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.spec.ts` (whole-object expectation at `:68-109` gains `projectCode: true`). Wiring `repoCredentials` into `ThreadHostDeps`/daemon belongs to US-007; this story only provides `RepoCredentialProvider` on `CredentialBroker`.

**Scope** — In: assign-parser projectRepos/projectReposUnavailable, TokenCache per-repo keys/ordering/apply, buildSyncRequest, socketPathFor, CredentialBroker acquireRepo/releaseRepo, probe capability. Out: ThreadHostDeps/daemon wiring and runProject use (US-007), mirror store (US-006), code tools (US-005).

**Interface**
```typescript
interface RepoCredentialProvider {
  acquireRepo(job: JobRow, repo: { repoId: string; cloneUrl: string }, options: AcquireOptions): Promise<AcquireResult>
  releaseRepo(job: JobRow, repoId: string): Promise<void>
}
socketPathFor(dir, runnerId, jobId, leaseEpoch, repoId?)
TokenCache.want/wanted/drop(jobId, leaseEpoch, repoId?)  TokenCache.state(jobId, leaseEpoch, nowMs, repoId?)
```
acceptanceCriteria: `parseAssign` on a PROJECT `SESSION` THREAD ASSIGN with `projectRepos: [{ repoId: 'r1', owner: 'o', name: 'n', defaultBranch: 'main', cloneUrl: 'https://github.com/o/n.git' }]` and `projectReposUnavailable: [{ owner: 'o', name: 'g', reason: 'no installation' }]` returns `ok: true` with both arrays copied onto `assign.thread`.

`parseAssign` returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid project repos' }` for `projectRepos` that is not an array, that holds 11 entries, or that holds an entry with repoId `../x`, owner `a//b`, name `a/b`, an empty `defaultBranch`, cloneUrl `file:///tmp/x`, or cloneUrl `http://github.com/o/n.git` (one table-driven test).
`parseAssign` returns `invalid project repos` for `projectReposUnavailable` with 51 entries or with an entry whose reason is `other`, and for `projectRepos` on a REPO thread ASSIGN.
`parseAssign` of a PROJECT ASSIGN without `projectRepos` returns `ok: true` with no `projectRepos` key on the thread.

A `TokenCache` with `want('j1', 1)` and `want('j1', 1, 'r1')` returns two requests from `requests`: one `{ jobId: 'j1', leaseEpoch: 1 }` with no `repoId` key and one `{ jobId: 'j1', leaseEpoch: 1, repoId: 'r1' }`.

A `TokenCache` with 70 repository entries wanted first and then one entry without `repoId` returns 64 requests from `requests`, the entry without `repoId` first, followed by the first 63 repository entries in want order.
`TokenCache.apply` with a token carrying `repoId: 'r1'` for job `j1` makes `state('j1', 1, now, 'r1')` a token and leaves `state('j1', 1, now)` pending.

`TokenCache.apply` with a `GitTokenError` `{ jobId: 'j1', repoId: 'r1', reason: 'repo_not_assigned' }` makes `state('j1', 1, now, 'r1')` the error `repo_not_assigned`; `drop('j1', 1, 'r1')` then makes `wanted('j1', 1, 'r1')` false and leaves `wanted('j1', 1)` true.
`buildSyncRequest` with a token request `{ jobId: 'j1', leaseEpoch: 1, repoId: 'r1' }` sends it with `repoId: 'r1'`, and a request without `repoId` is sent without the key.

`socketPathFor(dir, 'run', 'j1', 1)` is `dir` joined with the first 16 hex characters of the sha256 of `run:j1:1` plus `.sock`, and `socketPathFor(dir, 'run', 'j1', 1, 'r1')` uses the sha256 of `run:j1:1:r1`.

`CredentialBroker.acquireRepo(job, { repoId: 'r1', cloneUrl: 'https://github.com/o/n.git' }, { wait: true })` after the cache receives a token for `(j1, 1, 'r1')` resolves `ok: true` with a helper and `binDir: null`, and running that helper's `get` for `protocol=https` and `host=github.com` prints that token as the password.
The helper from `acquireRepo` prints no credentials for a `get` with `host=gitlab.com`.
After `releaseRepo(job, 'r1')`, `wanted('j1', 1, 'r1')` is false and the helper's `get` prints no credentials; `release(job)` on a job with two acquired repositories makes both repositories unwanted.
`NaxCapabilityProbe.probe` reports `projectCode: true` in its capabilities.

routing.reasoning: Credential brokering and token cache keying (security override); must leave repoId-less behavior byte-identical.

suggestedCriteria: `CredentialBroker.acquireRepo` with `wait: true` resolves `{ ok: false, reason: 'cancelled' }` when `isCancelled` returns true before a token arrives.
`CredentialBroker.acquire` for a job without `repoId` still serves the socket at the path `socketPathFor(dir, runnerId, jobId, leaseEpoch)` and writes the `gh`/`glab` shims, unchanged.

modifiedFiles.reason: its whole-object capability expectation at `:68-109` gains `projectCode: true`; other expectations unchanged.

outOfScope: Wiring `repoCredentials` into `ThreadHostDeps` and the daemon, and calling `acquireRepo` from `runProject`, belong to US-007.

userStories.title: Runner code tools over pinned mirrors
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `buildProjectCodeTools`, four read-only tools (`list_repos`, `list_files`, `search_repo`, `read_file`) that read git objects at pinned shas.

**Motivation** — The agent needs to answer cross-repository code questions without any checkout.

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

- 1c-b-D13 (code tools): a new `apps/runner/src/thread/project-code/code-tools.ts` exports `buildProjectCodeTools(ctx: ProjectCodeToolContext): EmbedderTool[]` returning, in this order, `list_repos`, `list_files`, `search_repo`, `read_file`, with `ProjectCodeToolContext { pins: readonly ProjectCodePin[]; unavailable: readonly { repo: string; reason: string }[]; git: Git; searchTimeoutMs: number; nowMs: () => number }` and `ProjectCodePin { repo: string; sha: string; gitDir: string }` (`repo` is `owner/name`). Every tool has `approval: 'never'` and runs through `refuseInvalidInput` (`apps/runner/src/thread/tools/shared.ts:33`). Every git call uses `cwd: pin.gitDir`, `env { GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1' }` and `timeoutMs: searchTimeoutMs`. A `repo` that names no pin answers the error result `unknown repo`.
  - `list_repos {}`: one line per pin, `owner/name @ <sha first 7>`, then one line per unavailable entry, `owner/name unavailable (<reason>)`. With neither: `no repositories`.
  - `list_files { repo, dir?, glob? }`: `git ls-tree -r -z --name-only <sha>`; `dir` (checked with `assertRelativePath`) keeps paths under `dir/`; `glob` (checked with `checkGlob`) keeps paths that `new Bun.Glob(glob).match(path)` accepts; at most 2000 entries plus `[truncated: N more]`, then `joinCapped(lines, 262144, false)`, as `list-files.ts` does.
  - `search_repo { repo?, pattern, fixed?, glob?, max? }`: `pattern`, `fixed`, `max` and `glob` are checked as `search-repo.ts` checks them; runs `git -c core.quotePath=false grep -n -I --no-color (-F|-E) -e <pattern> <sha> [-- :(glob)<glob>]` on the named pin, or on every pin in pin order when `repo` is absent; exit 1 is no match. Each hit line `<sha>:<path>:<line>:<text>` is emitted as `owner/name:<path>:<line>:<text>`. Hits are capped at `max` (default 200, at most 200) in total and joined with `joinCapped(lines, 65536, total > max)` where `total` is the number of hits found before the cap; no hit answers `no matches`; a search whose elapsed time reaches `searchTimeoutMs` answers the error result `search timed out` (the rule `search-repo.ts:44` uses).
  - `read_file { repo, path, startLine?, endLine? }`: `path` checked with `assertRelativePath`; `startLine` and `endLine` integers of at least 1 with `endLine >= startLine` (else `invalid lines`), `startLine` defaulting to 1; `git ls-tree -z <sha> -- <path>` printing no entry answers `not found`, and an entry whose type is not `blob` or whose mode is `120000` (a symlink) answers `not a file`; the content is read with `git cat-file blob <sha>:<path>`, and content that holds a NUL character in its first 8000 characters answers `binary file`. With `n` lines, a `startLine` above `n` answers `invalid lines` (for an empty file, any `startLine` above 1 does). The result is the header `owner/name:<path>@<sha7> lines <a>-<b> of <n>` followed by lines `a` to `b` (default the whole file, `b` clamped to `n`; an empty file gives `lines 0-0 of 0` and no lines), header and lines together joined with `joinCapped([header, ...lines], 65536, false)`.

Helpers available: `assertRelativePath` (`apps/runner/src/paths/safe-segment.ts:35`); `checkGlob`, `joinCapped`, `refused`, `refuseInvalidInput`, `fieldOf`, `InvalidToolInput` (`apps/runner/src/thread/tools/shared.ts`); `Git.run(args, { cwd, timeoutMs?, env?, credentialHelper? })` resolves `{ code, stdout, stderr }`; test helpers `isolateGit`, `git`, `makeOrigin`, `pushCommit` in `apps/runner/test/helpers/git-fixture.ts`.

**Scope** — In: code-tools.ts and its tests against real bare repos. Out: mirror creation/refresh (US-006), session-start wiring (US-007).

**Interface**
```typescript
interface ProjectCodePin { repo: string; sha: string; gitDir: string }
interface ProjectCodeToolContext {
  pins: readonly ProjectCodePin[]
  unavailable: readonly { repo: string; reason: string }[]
  git: Git
  searchTimeoutMs: number
  nowMs: () => number
}
buildProjectCodeTools(ctx: ProjectCodeToolContext): EmbedderTool[]
```
acceptanceCriteria: `buildProjectCodeTools` returns tools named, in order, `list_repos`, `list_files`, `search_repo`, `read_file`, each with `approval` `never`.

`list_repos` with pins `o/a` at sha `abcdef1234…` and an unavailable entry `{ repo: 'o/g', reason: 'no installation' }` returns the lines `o/a @ abcdef1` and `o/g unavailable (no installation)`; with no pins and no unavailable entries it returns `no repositories`.
`list_files { repo: 'o/a' }` returns every file path of the pinned commit, and a file added in a later commit of the same repository is not listed.
`list_files { repo: 'o/a', dir: 'src' }` returns only paths under `src/`, and `{ repo: 'o/a', glob: '**/*.md' }` returns only Markdown paths.
`list_files { repo: 'o/z' }` for an unpinned repository returns the error result `unknown repo`, and `{ repo: 'o/a', dir: '../x' }` returns an error result.

`search_repo { repo: 'o/a', pattern: 'needle' }` returns hit lines of the form `o/a:<path>:<line>:<text>` with no sha in them, including a hit in a file whose path holds a non-ASCII character, printed unquoted.
`search_repo { pattern: 'needle' }` without `repo` returns hits of both pins `o/a` and `o/b`, those of `o/a` first.
`search_repo` with a pattern that matches nowhere returns `no matches` as a non-error result.
`search_repo { pattern: 'x', max: 2 }` over a commit with five matching lines returns two hit lines followed by `[truncated]`.
With a fake `Git` whose grep exits 128 after the injected clock passes `searchTimeoutMs`, `search_repo` returns the error result `search timed out`.
`read_file { repo: 'o/a', path: 'src/a.ts', startLine: 2, endLine: 3 }` returns the header `o/a:src/a.ts@<sha7> lines 2-3 of <n>` followed by exactly lines 2 and 3 of the pinned file content.
`read_file` returns the error result `not found` for a missing path, `not a file` for the path `src`, and `binary file` for a file holding a NUL byte (one table-driven test).

`read_file` returns the error result `invalid lines` for `startLine` 0, for `startLine` 1.5, for `startLine` 5 with `endLine` 4, and for `startLine` 50 on a 10-line file; on an empty file it returns only the header `o/a:<path>@<sha7> lines 0-0 of 0`.
`read_file` on a file of 200000 bytes returns at most 65536 bytes counting the header, ending with `[truncated]`.

routing.reasoning: One new file of four tools that mirror existing REPO thread tools (list-files, search-repo) using shared helpers; read-only, self-contained and testable against real bare repos.

suggestedCriteria: `read_file` returns the error result `not a file` for a symlink entry (mode 120000).
outOfScope: Tool results with code are neither masked nor fenced, as REPO thread tool results are not.
Creating or refreshing mirrors (US-006) and opening the session with these tools (US-007).

userStories.title: Runner mirror store and prune
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the shallow bare mirror store (`refreshMirror`, `projectCodeDirFor`) with sha pinning, a mirror prune, and wire the prune into the daemon's thread prune with a single shared `RepoMutex`.

**Motivation** — Each repository needs one shallow bare mirror shared by every thread on the runner, whose pinned objects stay reachable for the live session and are reclaimed afterwards.

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

- 1c-b-D12 (mirror store): a new `apps/runner/src/thread/project-code/mirror-store.ts` exports `projectCodeDirFor(homeDir: string, repoId: string): string` (`<homeDir>/project-code/<repoId>.git`, `repoId` passed through `assertSegment`) and `refreshMirror(input: { git: Git; mutex: Pick<RepoMutex, 'acquire'>; homeDir: string; repo: ProjectRepoAssign; credentialHelper: string | null; timeoutMs: number; nowMs: () => number; allowFileProtocol?: boolean }): Promise<{ ok: true; sha: string } | { ok: false; reason: 'fetch timeout' | 'fetch failed' }>`. Under `mutex.acquire('project-code:' + repoId)` (a key no job uses, so it never waits on a RUN job) it creates the directory with `git init --bare -q` when absent, runs `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c gc.auto=0 -c protocol.file.allow=<never|always> fetch --depth 1 --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules <cloneUrl> +refs/heads/<defaultBranch>:refs/koda/tip` with `cwd` the mirror, `env { GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1' }`, the helper and `timeoutMs`, then reads `git rev-parse refs/koda/tip`, records the pin with `git update-ref refs/koda/pins/<pinId> <sha>`, writes the current time to `<mirror>/koda-last-used`, and returns the sha. The input gains `pinId: string` (the job id, passed through `assertSegment`). `protocol.file.allow` is `always` only when `allowFileProtocol` is true, which only tests pass. A non-zero fetch whose elapsed time by `nowMs` is at least `timeoutMs` answers `fetch timeout` (the rule `search-repo.ts:44` uses); any other non-zero exit answers `fetch failed`. Every pinned sha stays reachable from its pin ref, so neither a newer fetch nor `git gc` removes the objects a live session reads.
- 1c-b-D15 (mirror prune): a new `pruneProjectCode(input: { homeDir: string; git: Git; mutex: Pick<RepoMutex, 'acquire'>; nowMs: number; ttlMs: number; activeJobIds: ReadonlySet<string> }): Promise<void>` in `apps/runner/src/thread/project-code/mirror-prune.ts` visits every `<homeDir>/project-code/<repoId>.git` directory under `mutex.acquire('project-code:' + repoId)` and, holding it: deletes each `refs/koda/pins/<pinId>` whose `pinId` is not in `activeJobIds`; then, when no pin ref is left and the mirror's `koda-last-used` time (or, when that file is missing, the directory's mtime) is older than `ttlMs`, deletes the mirror; otherwise runs `git gc --prune=now -q` in it, which keeps every object a remaining pin reaches. The daemon's `pruneThreadAssets` (`daemon.ts:137-148`) calls it with `activeJobIds` the ids of the active journal jobs whose `command` is `THREAD`, the daemon's single `RepoMutex`, and `ttlMs` from `tuning.projectCodeMirrorTtlMs` (default 14 days). A failure is logged as a warning `project code prune failed` and does not stop the thread prune. The daemon creates that one `RepoMutex` before `pruneThreadAssets` is defined (today it is created inline at `daemon.ts:193`) and passes the same instance to the `Supervisor`, which hands it to every `ThreadJobRun` as `ThreadRunDeps.mutex`, so refresh and prune exclude each other.
- `Tuning` interface (`apps/runner/src/daemon/tuning.ts`) and the frozen `TUNING` object (`:57`) gain `projectCodeFetchTimeoutMs: 120_000` and `projectCodeMirrorTtlMs: 1_209_600_000`; `apps/runner/src/daemon/tuning.spec.ts` exact `TUNING` expectation (`toEqual` at `:6`) gains `projectCodeFetchTimeoutMs: 120000` and `projectCodeMirrorTtlMs: 1209600000` (the frozen-object assertion is unchanged).

Helpers: `Git.run(args, { cwd, timeoutMs?, env?, credentialHelper? })`; `RepoMutex.acquire(key): Promise<() => void>` (`apps/runner/src/supervisor/repo-mutex.ts:5`); `assertSegment` (`paths/safe-segment.ts:14`); existing `fetch --depth 1` example in `thread/skill-fetch.ts:118`; test helpers `isolateGit`, `git`, `makeOrigin`, `pushCommit`, `makeTempDirs`.

**Scope** — In: mirror-store.ts, mirror-prune.ts, tuning fields, daemon pruneThreadAssets wiring and single shared RepoMutex. Out: using refreshMirror from runProject and passing `repoCredentials` to the thread host (US-007), code tools (US-005).

**Interface**
```typescript
projectCodeDirFor(homeDir: string, repoId: string): string
refreshMirror(input: { git: Git; mutex: Pick<RepoMutex, 'acquire'>; homeDir: string; repo: ProjectRepoAssign; credentialHelper: string | null; timeoutMs: number; nowMs: () => number; allowFileProtocol?: boolean; pinId: string }): Promise<{ ok: true; sha: string } | { ok: false; reason: 'fetch timeout' | 'fetch failed' }>
pruneProjectCode(input: { homeDir: string; git: Git; mutex: Pick<RepoMutex, 'acquire'>; nowMs: number; ttlMs: number; activeJobIds: ReadonlySet<string> }): Promise<void>
```
acceptanceCriteria: `refreshMirror` against a `file://` origin with `allowFileProtocol: true` creates `<home>/project-code/<repoId>.git` as a bare repository and resolves `{ ok: true, sha }` with `sha` the origin's `main` tip.

After a new commit is pushed to the origin, a second `refreshMirror` resolves the new tip sha, and the first sha's file content is still readable from the mirror with `git cat-file blob <first sha>:<path>`.
`refreshMirror` with `pinId` `j1` leaves the ref `refs/koda/pins/j1` pointing at the resolved sha and writes `koda-last-used` with the current time.
`refreshMirror` without `allowFileProtocol` against a `file://` origin resolves `{ ok: false, reason: 'fetch failed' }`.
`refreshMirror` with a fake `Git` whose fetch exits 137 once the injected clock has passed `timeoutMs` resolves `{ ok: false, reason: 'fetch timeout' }`.
`refreshMirror` acquires the mutex key `project-code:<repoId>` before its first git call and releases it after its last.
`refreshMirror` with `repoId` `../x` rejects with a path error and runs no git command.
A mirror refreshed with `pinId` `j1` at sha X and then with `pinId` `j2` at a newer sha Y still serves `git cat-file blob X:<path>` after `pruneProjectCode` runs with `activeJobIds` holding `j1`.
`pruneProjectCode` with `activeJobIds` empty deletes `refs/koda/pins/j1` and `refs/koda/pins/j2`, and runs `git gc --prune=now -q` in a mirror whose `koda-last-used` time is recent.
`pruneProjectCode` deletes a mirror with no remaining pin ref whose `koda-last-used` time is older than `ttlMs`.
`pruneProjectCode` keeps a mirror whose `koda-last-used` time is older than `ttlMs` while it holds the pin ref of a job in `activeJobIds`.
`pruneProjectCode` acquires the mutex key `project-code:<repoId>` for each mirror it visits.
The daemon's thread prune, with one active THREAD job `j1`, calls `pruneProjectCode` with `activeJobIds` holding `j1` and with the same `RepoMutex` instance the daemon gives its `Supervisor`.
When `pruneProjectCode` rejects, the daemon's thread prune logs the warning `project code prune failed` and still calls `pruneThreads`.

routing.reasoning: Git object lifetime (pin refs vs gc), mutex exclusion between refresh and prune, and daemon wiring change; real-git tests.

modifiedFiles.reason: its exact `TUNING` expectation (`toEqual` at `:6`) gains `projectCodeFetchTimeoutMs: 120000` and `projectCodeMirrorTtlMs: 1209600000`; the frozen-object assertion is unchanged.

outOfScope: Calling `refreshMirror` from `runProject` and passing `repoCredentials` to the thread host belong to US-007.

userStories.title: Runner PROJECT session start with code
userStories.description:
Every case below runs `ThreadJobRun` on a PROJECT `SESSION` ASSIGN with the fake host of `test/unit/thread-job-run-project.spec.ts`, a stub `repoCredentials` and a stub `refreshMirror` on the host.

**Goal** — Make `ThreadJobRun.runProject` acquire per-repository tokens, refresh and pin mirrors, release the tokens, and open the PROJECT session with the code tools.

**Motivation** — This joins the API's ASSIGN, the per-repository credentials, the mirrors and the tools into a working PROJECT session that degrades per repository.

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

- 1c-b-R3: the pinned repositories and shas reach the agent through a `list_repos` tool, not through the instructions.
- 1c-b-R5 (partial failure): a repository whose token or fetch fails is unavailable for that session; the session still starts with the rest. A session whose every repository failed still starts: it has no pins, and `list_repos` lists each repository as unavailable.
- 1c-b-D11 (tail): `ThreadHostDeps` (`thread-job-run.ts:67-88`) gains the optional `repoCredentials?: RepoCredentialProvider`; the daemon passes the broker (`daemon.ts:180-191`). Without it a PROJECT session runs as today.
- 1c-b-D14 (session start): `ThreadJobRun.runProject` (`thread-job-run.ts:369-415`), after `setUpSkills`, when `thread.projectRepos` is present and `deps.host.repoCredentials` is set:
  1. calls `repoCredentials.acquireRepo(row, { repoId, cloneUrl }, { wait: true, isCancelled })` for every listed repository concurrently, so every token is wanted before any wait, with `isCancelled` polling the cancel request and a halt as the REPO path does (`:275`);
  2. refreshes the repositories that got credentials, at most 3 at a time (`PROJECT_CODE_FETCH_CONCURRENCY = 3`), each through `deps.host.refreshMirror ?? refreshMirror` with `mutex: this.deps.mutex` (the run's existing `ThreadRunDeps.mutex`, `thread-job-run.ts:119-122`), `pinId` the job id, its own helper and `timeoutMs = tuning.projectCodeFetchTimeoutMs ?? 120000`;
  3. calls `releaseRepo` for every acquired repository whatever the fetch returned;
  4. builds the pins (`gitDir` = `projectCodeDirFor`) and the unavailable list: each failed repository with reason `token: <acquire reason>`, `fetch timeout` or `fetch failed`, followed by `thread.projectReposUnavailable` mapped to `{ repo: owner/name, reason }`;
  5. opens the session with `buildProjectThreadTools(...)`, then `buildProjectCodeTools(...)`, then the koda proxies.
  A halt during steps 1-3 releases the acquired repositories and ends with no transition; a cancel request during steps 1-3 releases them and ends the run `CANCELLED` with `cancelled before start`. Without `projectRepos`, or without `repoCredentials`, the run is exactly as today. `ThreadHostDeps` gains the optional `refreshMirror?: typeof refreshMirror` (tests inject a stub, as `prepareWorktree` is injected today) and `ThreadRunTuning` gains the optional `projectCodeFetchTimeoutMs?: number`. A PROJECT session with repositories is the one THREAD run that takes the repo mutex (only under `project-code:` keys); the comment at `thread-job-run.ts:115-117` is updated to say so.

The session worktree stays the thread's scratch directory. The daemon (`daemon.ts:180-191`) builds the thread host with `repoCredentials` set to its `CredentialBroker` and the daemon's `Tuning` supplies `projectCodeFetchTimeoutMs`. Tests build on the fake host of `apps/runner/test/unit/thread-job-run-project.spec.ts`; the real-git end-to-end test uses `makeOrigin` and `allowFileProtocol: true`.

**Scope** — In: runProject flow, ThreadHostDeps/ThreadRunTuning additions, daemon passing the broker, mutex comment, new spec file. Out: acquireRepo/releaseRepo implementation (US-004), refreshMirror/prune implementation (US-006), tool implementations (US-005).

**Interface**
```typescript
// ThreadHostDeps additions
repoCredentials?: RepoCredentialProvider
refreshMirror?: typeof refreshMirror
// ThreadRunTuning addition
projectCodeFetchTimeoutMs?: number
const PROJECT_CODE_FETCH_CONCURRENCY = 3
```
acceptanceCriteria: With two `projectRepos`, the run calls `acquireRepo` once per repository with its `repoId` and `cloneUrl`, and both calls start before either resolves.
With two `projectRepos` and both refreshes succeeding, the run calls `releaseRepo` once per repository before `sessions.open` is called.

With both refreshes succeeding, the session opens with tools named `load_skill`, `read_skill_file`, `list_repos`, `list_files`, `search_repo`, `read_file`, in that order, and its `worktree` is the thread's scratch directory.
Each `refreshMirror` call receives the run's `mutex`, `pinId` equal to the job id, the helper its `acquireRepo` returned, and `timeoutMs` 120000 when `projectCodeFetchTimeoutMs` is not set.

When `acquireRepo` resolves `{ ok: false, reason: 'git token: repo_not_assigned' }` for one repository, the session still opens, `refreshMirror` is not called for it, and `list_repos` returns it as `unavailable (token: git token: repo_not_assigned)` and the other as pinned.
When `acquireRepo` resolves `{ ok: false, reason: 'git token: timeout' }` for a repository, `list_repos` returns it as `unavailable (token: git token: timeout)`.
When every refresh resolves `{ ok: false, reason: 'fetch failed' }`, the session still opens, `list_repos` lists each repository as `unavailable (fetch failed)`, and the job transitions to RUNNING.
The ASSIGN's `projectReposUnavailable` entries appear in `list_repos` after the run's own failures, with their reasons.
A cancel request while `acquireRepo` is waiting ends the run `CANCELLED` with reason `cancelled before start`, calls `releaseRepo` for each repository, and opens no session.

A cancel request while `refreshMirror` is running ends the run `CANCELLED` with reason `cancelled before start` after the refresh settles, calls `releaseRepo` for each repository, and opens no session.
A halt while `refreshMirror` is running calls `releaseRepo` for each repository after the refresh settles, opens no session, and records no job transition.

A PROJECT ASSIGN without `projectRepos`, and one with `projectRepos` on a host without `repoCredentials`, open the session with only `load_skill` and `read_skill_file` plus koda proxies, and call no `acquireRepo`.
With five `projectRepos`, at most 3 `refreshMirror` calls are in flight at once.
The daemon builds the thread host with `repoCredentials` set to its `CredentialBroker`.

With a real bare origin from `makeOrigin` and a host `refreshMirror` that calls the real `refreshMirror` with `allowFileProtocol: true`, the opened session's `list_repos` reports the origin's tip sha and its `read_file` returns the origin's file content at that sha.

routing.reasoning: Orchestrates credentials, bounded-concurrency fetch, cancel/halt cleanup and tool assembly in the run state machine; touches token lifecycle so cleanup ordering matters.

userStories.title: Web project-code notice
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Show a notice on a live PROJECT thread session whose runner cannot read project code.

**Motivation** — Placement does not require `projectCode`, so a session on a runner without it has no code tools and the user must be told (as for `kodaTools`).

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

- 1c-b-D16 (web notice): `apps/web/lib/thread-handoff.ts` gains `showProjectCodeNotice(thread: ThreadDetailDto): boolean` (true when `thread.session?.state === 'live'` and `projectCodeUnavailableOn` is set), and a new `ThreadProjectCodeNotice.vue`, mounted on `pages/[project]/threads/[id].vue` next to `ThreadKodaToolsNotice`, renders `fleet.threads.projectCode.unavailable` with `{ runner }` (en: `project code is unavailable on runner {runner}; this session cannot read the project's repositories.`, zh: `此运行器 {runner} 上无法读取项目代码；此会话无法读取项目的代码仓库。`). `ThreadSession` (`apps/web/lib/thread-types.ts:48-60`) gains `projectCodeUnavailableOn?: string`.

The test id is `thread-project-code-notice`. Mirror `components/fleet/threads/ThreadKodaToolsNotice.vue` and `showKodaToolsNotice` (`lib/thread-handoff.ts:37-39`); notice mount at `pages/[project]/threads/[id].vue:89-91`; web i18n lives in `apps/web/i18n/locales/{en,zh}.json` (separate from API i18n).

**Scope** — In: showProjectCodeNotice, ThreadProjectCodeNotice.vue, ThreadSession field, en/zh strings, page mount. Out: API session field (US-003), rendering code citations as links.

**Interface**
```typescript
showProjectCodeNotice(thread: ThreadDetailDto): boolean
// ThreadSession: projectCodeUnavailableOn?: string
// i18n key: fleet.threads.projectCode.unavailable ({ runner })
```
acceptanceCriteria: `showProjectCodeNotice` returns true for a thread whose session state is `live` and whose `projectCodeUnavailableOn` is `wk-mac`.
`showProjectCodeNotice` returns false when the session is `closed`, when `projectCodeUnavailableOn` is absent, and when there is no session (one table-driven test).

Mounting `ThreadProjectCodeNotice` with a live session whose `projectCodeUnavailableOn` is `wk-mac` renders an element with test id `thread-project-code-notice` whose text is the English `fleet.threads.projectCode.unavailable` message with `wk-mac` in place of `{runner}`.
Mounting `ThreadProjectCodeNotice` for a live session without `projectCodeUnavailableOn` renders no `thread-project-code-notice` element.
Translating `fleet.threads.projectCode.unavailable` with `{ runner: 'wk-mac' }` returns a message holding `wk-mac` in the `en` locale and in the `zh` locale.
Mounting the thread page `pages/[project]/threads/[id].vue` for a PROJECT thread whose live session holds `projectCodeUnavailableOn: 'wk-mac'` renders the `thread-project-code-notice` element.

routing.reasoning: Direct mirror of the existing ThreadKodaToolsNotice component, helper and i18n keys.

analysis:
Feature 3b of fleet S5b (S5b-R15): a PROJECT thread's agent reads the code of every GitHub fleet repository of its project, read-only, pinned at session start. Flow: API placement adds projectRepos/projectReposUnavailable to the THREAD ASSIGN (only for PROJECT+SESSION on a runner with capabilities.projectCode) -> runner requests a read-only per-repository GitHub token through sync (repoId on TokenRequest) -> API fence recomputes the fetchable repo set (fetchableProjectRepos(findProjectRepos(job.projectId))) and mints via GitTokenBroker.mint({readOnly:true}) -> runner fetches a shallow bare mirror per repo under <home>/project-code/<repoId>.git, pins the tip sha under refs/koda/pins/<jobId>, and exposes four tools (list_repos, list_files, search_repo, read_file) reading git objects at the pinned sha. No checkout, no worktree.

Key files (api): apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/github-app-client.ts (mintInstallationToken :61-72, add mintReadOnlyToken), git-token.broker.ts (mint :30-45, fresh, evict), common/capabilities-core.ts (:118-165, add projectCode like kodaTools), common/thread-jobs.ts (runtime mirror of protocol constants, THREAD_LIMITS :24; the api reads @nathapp/fleet-protocol with import type only, see common/protocol.spec.ts:36-41), sync/sync.service.ts (sync :54, grantTokens :112-141), sync/sync-request.parser.ts (parseTokenRequest :58-61), jobs/placement.service.ts (placeJob :62, assign :189-202, withKodaTools :211-214), jobs/prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts + jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts (IFleetJobRepository :214; gains findThreadTokenScope and findProjectRepos; only implementer is PrismaFleetJobRepository), threads/ingest/prisma-thread-ingest.repository.ts (session_started :419-433, kodaToolsUnavailableOn notice :472-480, close/failure keep rule :442-448), threads/thread-instructions.ts (:41-49), thread.dto.ts session schema :27, chat-thread.domain.ts :50-51.

Key files (runner): supervisor/assign-parser.ts (cleanKodaTools :96-110, thread block :173-224), credentials/token-cache.ts, credentials/broker.ts, credentials/socket-dir.ts (:21-24), sync/batch.ts (:74), capabilities/nax-probe.ts (:165-174), thread/thread-job-run.ts (runProject :369-415, REPO credential wait :275, ThreadHostDeps :67-88, ThreadRunTuning :90-108, mutex comment :115-117), thread/tools/{list-files,search-repo,shared}.ts, paths/safe-segment.ts, thread/skill-fetch.ts (:118 fetch --depth 1), thread/thread-prune.ts, daemon/daemon.ts (pruneThreadAssets :137-148, thread host :180-191, inline RepoMutex :193), daemon/tuning.ts (TUNING :57). Web: lib/thread-handoff.ts (showKodaToolsNotice :37-39), components/fleet/threads/ThreadKodaToolsNotice.vue, pages/[project]/threads/[id].vue (:89-91), lib/thread-types.ts (:48-60), i18n locales en/zh.

Protocol package packages/fleet-protocol: all changes are additive/optional (ProjectRepoAssign, ProjectRepoUnavailable, PROJECT_CODE_LIMITS, ThreadAssign.projectRepos/projectReposUnavailable, repoId? on TokenRequest/GitToken/GitTokenError, RunnerCapabilities.projectCode?: true). FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION unchanged. US-001 owns these edits; later stories compile against them.

Risks: (1) Security: token fence must never mint for a repo outside the recomputed fetchable set; read-only permission set exactly contents:read + metadata:read; evict must drop ro entries; repo-scoped sockets must answer only for the clone URL protocol/host and write no gh/glab shims. (2) Backward compat: requests/entries without repoId must behave exactly as today (cache keys, socket path hash, requests ordering, batch projection). (3) Concurrency: mirror refresh and prune share one daemon RepoMutex instance under key 'project-code:<repoId>'; daemon must create the RepoMutex before pruneThreadAssets and pass the same instance to Supervisor. (4) Ordering: fetchableProjectRepos and withProjectRepos must use the same walk so ASSIGN and fence agree. (5) US-003 regenerates openapi.json (bun run api:export-spec) and apps/cli/src/generated (bun run generate); never hand-edit generated files. (6) Existing tests broken by correct change: thread-instructions.spec.ts, prisma-thread-ingest.repository.spec.ts fake thread row (add kind), nax-probe.spec.ts, tuning.spec.ts. (7) nax runs touching apps/api need the compose test Postgres (bun run test:db:up in apps/api) for [integration] ACs. (8) .nax/mono/apps/runner/context.md is updated by hand, not by a story. Tests: api vitest (*.spec.ts, integration under test/integration), runner bun:test with real git fixtures (test/helpers/git-fixture.ts, tmp.ts), web jest.
outOfScope: GitLab repositories are not read by PROJECT threads (1c-b-R2): koda's GitLab access is a stored project token whose scope it cannot narrow, so GitLab read-only access is deferred to a later feature; GitLab repositories are listed as unavailable `not a GitHub repository`.
WORKSPACE threads never read code (S5b-R13); they are feature S5b-1d.
A session never re-fetches: the shas pinned at session start hold until the session ends.
REPO threads are unchanged: they keep their worktree and their five tools, and see no other repository.
PROJECT threads get no `write_doc`, no Publish, no Plan and no Run.
Code indexing, embeddings, a reranker and repository docs search are feature S5b-1c-c and later.
Tool results with code are neither masked nor fenced, as REPO thread tool results are not; code is repository content the project's writers control.
Code citations (`owner/name:path@sha7`) are not rendered as links in the web.
RUN, PLAN and REPO thread jobs keep their own clones and never use the mirror store.
No new placement rule: a PROJECT session may land on a runner without `projectCode` and then has no code tools.
The sync request's 64-token-request cap is unchanged.
US-002 only: the read-only token is minted per request and cached per `(job, epoch, repository)`; no cross-job token sharing.
US-006 only: two runners never share a mirror; each runner keeps its own under its home directory.
The runner context file `.nax/mono/apps/runner/context.md` ("It never takes the repo mutex") is read-only to the run; it is updated by hand with this spec, not by a story.
